newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares dip with Europe, more falls up front.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares dip with Europe, more falls up front.

text.p: Danish share prices closed lower on Tuesday following the downward European trend after resisting for a while, with dealers seeing more falls ahead.
"The Danish stock market slipped with the rest of Europe, after holding out for a while in the morning. I cannot see any reason why we should not continue downwards on Wednesday." one dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index closed 1.24 point down at 130.10, while the KFX December future, due to expire on December 20, shed 0.60 point to 130.10 with 675 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
Tele Danmark was the day's most traded paper with 177,000 shares changing hands and closing two crowns lower at 304.
Danisco, which is to unveil its first-half 1996/97 result on Wednesday with analysts tipping improved interim profits, dropped five crowns to finish at 330.
Otherwise ISS closed four crowns down at 156, while leading banks Den Danske Bank and Unidanmark shed two and four crowns to finish at 448 and 294 respectively.
Overall turnover for the day was 1.023 billion crowns.
